map.name: script
map.takes: nothing
map.gives: a ready script with imports, credentials, and a prompt
map.text: script loads the tools, reads credentials with load_dotenv(), sets the PROMPT, and runs main() when called directly.

children.text: imports bring in the tools: ast, json, os, re, sys, Path, boto3, jedi, Config, and load_dotenv.
load_dotenv() reads the credentials from the .env file next to the script.
PROMPT instructs the model to merge cells into groups, give each a plain-English text, and return one JSON object.
main() runs when the script starts directly.

map.name: statements
map.takes: a file path and source text
map.gives: a list of (depth, start line, end line) tuples for every statement
map.text: statements() collects every statement in a .py source as a (depth, lineno, end_lineno) tuple by calling walk() on the parsed AST.

children.text: statements() returns an empty list for non-.py files and sets up the rows list.
statements() calls walk() on the parsed source and returns rows.

map.name: statements.walk
map.takes: an AST node and a depth integer
map.gives: rows entries of (depth, start line, end line) for every statement in the subtree
map.text: walk() recurses over every child node and appends a (depth, lineno, end_lineno) tuple to rows for each ast.stmt child.

map.name: cells_of
map.takes: a file path, source text, and numbered lines
map.gives: a list of span cells covering every non-blank line in the file
map.text: cells_of() splits a source file into span cells: one per AST statement leaf for Python files, with uncovered lines merged into the nearest span, or one per non-blank run for all other files.

children.text: cells_of() sets up spans and checks whether the file is Python.
cells_of() calls emit() on every top-level AST node to fill spans.
cells_of()'s fallback stage scans lines for non-blank runs and returns them as span cells when spans is empty.
cells_of() finds lines not covered by any span and collects them into extra runs.
cells_of() merges each extra run into the nearest span and returns the sorted span cells.

map.name: cells_of.kids_of
map.takes: an AST node
map.gives: a flat list of direct and indirect statement children
map.text: kids_of() collects all direct statement children of node, and recurses into non-statement children to find deeper ones.

map.name: cells_of.emit
map.takes: an AST node
map.gives: flat span entries in spans for every uncovered line run in node and its descendants
map.text: emit() walks node and its children: it calls kids_of(), recurses into each child, and appends to spans each run of lines that node owns but no child covers.

children.text: emit() gets the direct statement children of node by calling kids_of().
emit() adds the full node span to spans and returns when node has no children.
emit()'s second stage builds covered from each child's line range and recurses into each child with emit().
emit()'s third stage walks every line of node, finds lines not in covered, and appends each uncovered run to spans.

map.name: merge
map.takes: a list of [start, end] span pairs
map.gives: a sorted list of non-overlapping [start, end] spans
map.text: merge() joins overlapping or adjacent spans in sorted order into a flat list of non-overlapping ranges.

map.name: ask
map.takes: a prompt string
map.gives: a parsed JSON object from the model reply
map.text: ask() sends a prompt to the Bedrock model and returns the first JSON object from its text reply.

children.text: ask() opens a Bedrock runtime client with the AWS region and timeouts from the environment.
ask() sends the prompt to the model and asserts that stopReason is end_turn.
ask() extracts the text reply and returns its outermost JSON object.

map.name: check_pass
map.takes: a groups map, a cells list, statement ranges, blank lines, essential lines, and a bad-names set
map.gives: the validated groups list
map.text: check_pass() validates a groups map: the list is non-empty and shorter than cells, every group covers cells in order with a non-empty text and no bad function names, no statement is cut across a group boundary, and the last group ends at the final cell.

children.text: check_pass() reads the groups list, asserts it is a non-empty list shorter than cells, and sets at to 1.
check_pass() walks each group: asserts cell order, range, non-empty text, no bad function names, and at most 15 non-blank lines on a first pass.
check_pass() checks each statement against the group: asserts no statement is cut, then advances at.
check_pass() asserts the last group ends at the final cell and returns groups.

map.name: lift
map.takes: a list of groups and their source cells
map.gives: a flat list of merged nodes, each with layer, text, lines, and optional children
map.text: lift() turns a list of groups into a new node list: it passes a single already-texted cell through unchanged, or builds a new node with layer, text, and merged line spans from its kids.

children.text: lift() sets up the output list.

lift()'s main loop builds each output node: it passes a single already-texted cell through unchanged, or calls merge() to join its kids' line spans into a new node with layer, text, and optional children.
lift() returns the new list of merged nodes.

map.name: carve
map.takes: a line range a-b and a list of spans to exclude
map.gives: a sorted list of free sub-ranges with blank lines trimmed from each end
map.text: carve() cuts a line range into the free sub-ranges that the excluded spans do not cover, then trims blank lines from each end.

children.text: carve() sets up the used-line set, the spans list, and the run pointer.
carve() scans each position from a to b+1 and collects free runs into spans.
carve() trims blank lines from each span and appends non-empty ranges to out.
carve() returns the trimmed list of free ranges.

map.name: blocks_of
map.takes: a file path, its source text, and its lines
map.gives: a sorted list of block entries, each with a name, carved line spans, and an AST node
map.text: blocks_of() finds every function and script block in a source file: it calls grab() to collect function spans, calls carve() to cut inner and top-level ranges, and returns the blocks sorted by first line.

children.text: blocks_of() initializes fns by calling grab() on the parsed source if the file is a .py file.
blocks_of() builds a block entry for each function in fns by calling carve() to cut out its inner spans.
blocks_of() calls carve() on the full file range to find the top-level script lines and appends a script block if any remain.
blocks_of() sorts the blocks by their first line and returns them.

map.name: blocks_of.grab
map.takes: an AST node and a scope list
map.gives: entries appended to fns: name, span, and decorator start for every function and class found
map.text: grab() walks the AST from a node and records every function and class definition into fns with its name, full span, and decorator start line.

map.name: calls_of
map.takes: a block dict and a list of known names
map.gives: a sorted list of fully-qualified names that the block calls
map.text: calls_of() finds all names the block calls: it sets scope and out, runs scan() on the block's node or on each top-level body node, and returns out sorted.

children.text: calls_of() sets up: skip types, scope from block["name"], and an empty out set.
calls_of() calls scan() on block["node"] alone, or on every top-level body node that is not a skip type.
calls_of() returns out as a sorted list.

map.name: calls_of.resolve
map.takes: a short name and a scope list
map.gives: the full dotted name if found in names, or None
map.text: resolve() searches the scope chain from deepest to shallowest and returns the first matching full dotted name for word, or None.

map.name: calls_of.scan
map.takes: an AST node and a set of names to skip
map.gives: full dotted names added to out for each ast.Name that resolve() finds
map.text: scan() walks every child node, skips nested functions and classes, and adds to out the full name that resolve() returns for each ast.Name that is not the current block.

map.name: layers_of
map.takes: a list of blocks and a calls dict
map.gives: a dict mapping each block name to its call-depth integer
map.text: layers_of() maps every block name to its call-depth: it runs strong() on every unvisited block to find components, builds cross-component edges, then returns the height() of each block's component.

children.text: layers_of() sets up idx, low, on, st, comp, and k to run Tarjan's algorithm and build the call-depth map.
layers_of() calls strong() on every block name not yet visited to fill comp.
layers_of() builds edges: for each cross-component call in calls, it adds a directed edge between the component roots, then sets up h for height().
layers_of() returns a dict that maps each block name to the height() of its component.

map.name: layers_of.strong
map.takes: a node name v and the calls graph
map.gives: comp entries that map every node in v's SCC to its root
map.text: strong() runs Tarjan's algorithm on v: it records v, walks its neighbors to find back-edges, and collapses the stack into comp when v is the root of a strongly connected component.

children.text: strong()'s first stage records v in idx, low, st, and on, and sets its discovery index.
strong()'s second stage visits each neighbor w in calls[v]: recurses into w if unseen, then pulls low[w] or idx[w] back into low[v].
strong()'s third stage pops st down to v when low[v] equals idx[v], marks each popped node in comp, and stops at v.

map.name: layers_of.height
map.takes: a component key c
map.gives: the call-depth integer for c, cached in h
map.text: height() returns the call-depth of component c: 1 plus the maximum depth of its successors in edges, cached in h.

map.name: nodes_of
map.takes: a tree of nested node dicts
map.gives: a flat list of every node in depth-first order
map.text: nodes_of() calls walk() on tree and returns out, the flat list of every node in depth-first order.

map.name: nodes_of.walk
map.takes: a list of tree nodes
map.gives: a flat list of every node in depth-first order
map.text: walk() collects every node from ns into out and recurses into each node's children.

map.name: number
map.takes: a list of top-level tree nodes
map.gives: an id like F01 on each root node and a dotted id on each descendant
map.text: number() assigns a short id to each top-level node and calls walk() to give dotted ids to its children.

map.name: number.walk
map.takes: a list of child nodes
map.gives: a dotted id on each node and its descendants
map.text: walk() assigns a dotted id to each child node and recurses into its children.

map.name: owner_of
map.takes: a tree of nested node dicts
map.gives: a dict that maps each line number to the id of its leaf node
map.text: owner_of() maps every line number to its leaf node id by calling nodes_of() and scanning each leaf's line ranges into owner.

map.name: links
map.takes: a file path and a line-to-node-id owner map
map.gives: a list of rows with name, defining node id, and using node ids
map.text: links() finds every name defined in the .py file and returns the id of its definition node and the ids of all nodes that use it.

children.text: links() returns an empty list if the file is not a .py file.
links() resolves the file path and creates a jedi.Script for it.
links() sets up the empty rows list.

links() loops over every name in the script, skips names that go outside the file or have no owner, finds all in-file references via get_references(), and appends a row with the name, its defining node id, and the ids that use it.

map.name: row_of
map.takes: a cell index, a cell object, and the source lines
map.gives: a formatted string with the cell number, its line range, and its text or first source line
map.text: row_of() formats cell i as a numbered line range, with its text if it has one, or with its first source line if it does not.

map.name: write_node
map.takes: a tree node dict and an indentation string
map.gives: a JSON-like string for the node and its children
map.text: write_node() builds a string for one node: the id, optional name and call fields, text, lines, and a recursive children array.

children.text: write_node() opens the head string with the id field.
write_node() adds the name, layer, calls, takes, and gives fields when the node has a name, or only the layer field when it does not.
write_node() appends the text and lines fields to head.
write_node() returns head closed with a brace when the node has no children.
write_node() joins the children by calling write_node() on each, then returns head with the children array.

map.name: write_map
map.takes: a path and a map dict with file, links, and map keys
map.gives: a JSON file at path with the file name, links array, and map tree
map.text: write_map() writes the map to path as a single JSON object: the file name, the links array, and the map tree built by write_node().

children.text: write_map() formats the links array and calls write_node() for each map entry to build the tree string.
write_map() writes the full JSON object to path: the file name, the links array, and the map tree.

map.name: one_pass
map.takes: cells, prompt parts, layer, label, span, context, bad names, and a final flag
map.gives: a list with one merged node, or exits after 8 failed attempts
map.text: one_pass() sends the prompt to ask(), validates the reply with check_pass(), and returns the lifted or final node list, retrying up to 8 times on any rule violation.

children.text: one_pass()'s first stage formats the cell rows with row_of() and builds the base prompt from PROMPT.
one_pass() appends a final-pass instruction to base when final is true.
one_pass() initializes note, errs, and m before the retry loop.
one_pass() calls ask() with the prompt and note, then validates the reply with check_pass().
one_pass()'s final-pass branch checks that groups has one entry with takes and gives, builds a node with layer, text, takes, gives, and lines, attaches cells as children, and returns it.
one_pass() calls lift() to merge the groups into a new cell list and returns it.
one_pass()'s error handler prints the attempt number and label, appends the error to errs, and adds the last answer and all broken rules to note.
one_pass() exits the process when all 8 attempts fail.

map.name: compile_block
map.takes: a block descriptor, its cells, and prompt parts
map.gives: one compiled root node with text, takes, gives, and layer
map.text: compile_block() compiles one block into a single root node: it builds the statement list, label, and span, then calls one_pass() in a loop until one node with takes remains.

children.text: compile_block() filters bstmts to the block's lines, builds stext, label, and span, and sets layer to 0.
compile_block() calls one_pass() each iteration, incrementing layer and setting final when all cells have text, until one cell with takes remains.
compile_block() returns the single compiled root node.

map.name: main
map.takes: a source file path from the command line
map.gives: map.json next to the source file
map.text: main() turns one source file into map.json: a tree of texts over line ranges for every block, plus the links between names.

children.text: main()'s first stage reads the source file, splits it into lines, builds the numbered code string, and asserts the file is not empty.
main()'s second stage calls cells_of(), statements(), and builds blank and ess: the sets of blank lines and innermost statement lines.
main()'s third stage calls blocks_of(), calls_of(), and layers_of() to get blocks, calls, and lay.
main()'s fourth stage assigns each cell to its home block in parts.
main()'s fifth stage loops over blocks in layer order, builds ctx and bad for each, calls compile_block(), and stores the root node with name, layer, calls, and lines into done.
main()'s final stage sorts done into tree, calls number(), owner_of(), links(), and write_map() to write map.json, then prints the block, text, and link counts.
